directions.title: Speech-led analysis and review
directions.promiseGuidance: Make the central question clear early, support each material claim and return to the promised conclusion with its qualifications.
sectionGuidance: Let the introduction establish the question in the creator's natural voice.
In documentary-evidence sections, hold the original context long enough to read and distinguish observation from interpretation.
Let the conclusion resolve the promise without introducing unrelated visual distractions.
directions.rhythm: Follow the development of the argument. Remove confirmed repetition or filler while preserving complete words, natural cadence and meaningful pauses.
directions.visual: Keep the creator present when their reasoning or reaction matters. Use relevant demonstrations, comparisons and source documents when they improve comprehension.
directions.motion: Use selective support for concepts or calculations; reveal one informational step at a time and hold during reading.
directions.sound: Keep intelligible speech foremost. Music supports the current idea; purposeful sound can mark information arrivals without becoming an unsupported argument.
variants: A reflective section can stay still and quiet.
A dense comparison may use progressive graphics while reducing competing movement.
A short news opening may be brisk while the following analysis retains its own conversational cadence.
constraints: Preserve factual meaning, chronology, qualifications and the current creator intention.
Allow readable holds for text and evidence; keep captions legible and clear of important information.
Use high contrast, safe areas and accessible motion; avoid rapid flashes and prolonged shaking.
Diagnose source quality and delivery context before choosing technical processing.
Keep attribution and source context visible; this direction transfers no media rights or previous approval.
exclusions: Not a universal style or a fixed quota of cuts, graphics, music or sound effects.
Never manufacture evidence, reactions, chronology or certainty to create momentum.
Do not apply historical restoration settings or numeric mix targets without fresh source diagnosis.

directions.title: Step-by-step demonstration and tutorial
directions.promiseGuidance: Show the starting condition, necessary steps and observable result. Keep prerequisites, limitations and the current task clear.
sectionGuidance: Orient the viewer before an unfamiliar action.
Hold intermediate states and labels long enough to read or reproduce them.
Separate an explanation from the actual demonstrated result; preserve failed or conditional outcomes that affect the instructions.
directions.rhythm: Time the sequence to understanding and reproducibility. Give complex actions space instead of copying entertainment-oriented cutting.
directions.visual: Prefer the relevant interface, object or action at the moment it is explained. Use the creator's face when it clarifies intent, judgment or a transition.
directions.motion: Use a clear visual hierarchy and progressive annotation. Show beginning and ending states rather than animating over the essential action.
directions.sound: Keep instructions intelligible while preserving meaningful device, game or product sounds. Use cues for consequential actions, not every pointer movement.
variants: An experienced audience can use concise orientation while unfamiliar steps still receive clear holds.
A conceptual introduction can use analysis-style support before the practical sequence.
A troubleshooting branch can slow down to compare the observed and expected states.

directions.title: Narrative, documentary and conversation
directions.promiseGuidance: Establish the question or human experience and build toward an earned answer. Preserve chronology, uncertainty and the speaker's intended emotional tone.
sectionGuidance: Use orientation where a change in time, place or speaker would otherwise confuse the story.
Hold documentary material long enough to read and understand its provenance.
Give a consequential reflection room to settle; do not interrupt every emotional pause.
directions.rhythm: Follow causality, turns of thought and emotional space. A pause can carry meaning; remove it only when the source and editorial intent justify that choice.
directions.visual: Use relevant reactions, places and source material to establish context. Distinguish archival or illustrative imagery from direct evidence.
directions.motion: Use restrained orientation and emphasis around the story. Simplify competing movement when viewers must listen closely or read a document.
directions.sound: Keep conversation intelligible and preserve meaningful ambience. Musical or effect choices must not imply danger, guilt, scale or emotion unsupported by the record.
variants: A conversation-led section can favor sustained presence over graphic support.
An evidence-led section can use explanatory comparison while preserving source context.
A reflective ending may reduce sound and motion density instead of adding a forced climax.

directions.title: Focused short-form and highlights
directions.promiseGuidance: Deliver one complete point or moment with enough context to preserve meaning. The opening and ending must pay off the same promise.
sectionGuidance: Orient the viewer quickly without inventing a misleading hook.
Keep necessary labels and captions readable on the target display.
Preserve the setup and payoff of a joke, argument or demonstration rather than extracting a misleading isolated sentence.
directions.rhythm: Use concise progression suited to the source performance. Keep meaningful cadence and complete words; speed is not a requirement for every short.
directions.visual: Maintain one dominant focus. Reframe for the target aspect ratio while preserving faces, products, evidence and other relevant details.
directions.motion: Use selective emphasis with readable holds. Avoid continuous shaking, flashing or competing caption and graphic animations.
directions.sound: Prioritize the point or performance. Keep supporting music and effects from masking speech; preserve source-audio intent rather than forcing a constant sound bed.
variants: A practical highlight can use a compact demonstration sequence.
A reflective quote can remain quiet with minimal movement.
A longer parent-video section retains its own pacing; do not impose this short-form treatment on the whole film.
